name: Enzalutamide + Alisertib
item_2_mechanism:
Enzalutamide competitively blocks the Androgen Receptor (AR), which is the primary growth driver in castration-resistant prostate cancer. AR is expressed 3.4x higher in prostate than average tissue (PROSTATE-SELECTIVE). When AR is blocked, AR-dependent tumor cells stop proliferating and die. Healthy prostate cells are also affected but AR blockade is tolerable because prostate function is not essential for survival. 
Alisertib (MLN8237) inhibits Aurora Kinase A (AURKA), which has 122 protein interaction partners including TPX2, TACC3, MYCN. AURKA drives neuroendocrine transdifferentiation via the AURKA/N-MYC axis. When AR is blocked by enzalutamide, ~10-25% of tumor cells escape through NE differentiation. Alisertib blocks this escape route, trapping cells between AR blockade and NE blockade.

item_3_outcomes.honest: Escape route ODE uses estimated transition rates. Unified ODE alisertib combo collapsed (Cmax << EC50).

item_4_resistance.mechanism: 4-state escape: AR-dependent → AR-mutant (22%) + AR-V7 (15%) + NE-like (63%) at 2 years
item_4_resistance.drug_b_covers: NE-like escape cells (N state) via AURKA inhibition
item_4_resistance.uncovered: AR-mutant (T878A, F877L) and AR-V7 splice variants remain untargeted
item_4_resistance.honest: NE fraction 63% overpredicts vs clinical 10-25%. Transition rates estimated.

name: Olaparib + CHK1 inhibitor
item_2_mechanism:
Olaparib inhibits PARP1 (poly-ADP-ribose polymerase 1), which repairs single-strand DNA breaks. PARP1 is ubiquitous (UBIQUITOUS) — expressed in all cells. Selectivity comes from SYNTHETIC LETHALITY: cells with BRCA2 loss cannot repair double-strand breaks, so blocking single-strand repair (PARP) is lethal. BRCA2 is mutated in 8.0% of mCRPC (SU2C data). Healthy cells with intact BRCA2 tolerate PARP inhibition because they have backup repair. 
Prexasertib (CHK1i) inhibits CHK1 (checkpoint kinase 1), which is the DNA damage checkpoint. When PARP inhibition creates unrepaired DNA damage, CHK1 activates cell cycle arrest to buy repair time. Blocking CHK1 forces damaged cells into mitosis with unrepaired DNA → mitotic catastrophe → cell death. This closes the BRCA2 → CHEK1 escape route identified in our net analysis.

item_3_outcomes.honest: Not directly simulated in our ODE yet. PROfound data used as reference.

item_4_resistance.mechanism: BRCA2-loss synthetic lethality. Resistance via: BRCA2 reversion mutations, 53BP1 loss, ABCB1 efflux upregulation
item_4_resistance.escape_route: BRCA2 → CHEK1 (DNA damage checkpoint) identified in net analysis

name: Docetaxel (standard of care)
item_2_mechanism: Docetaxel stabilizes microtubules, blocking cell division in ALL actively dividing cancer cells. It is not selective — it kills both cancer and healthy dividing cells (hair follicles, gut lining, bone marrow). Efficacy comes from cancer cells dividing faster than healthy cells.

item_4_resistance.mechanism: Continuous resistance: cells along phenotype gradient survive proportionally to resistance level
